Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Today’s conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Mike Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Lee, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 was a strong quarter for NovaVolt Motors. We made significant progress in several key areas, including factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements, delivery volume guidance by model, battery costs per kWh and trends, total revenue and year-over-year growth, and average selling price trends by model and region. The demand for our NovaSUV continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of our new product launches is exceeding our initial expectations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our total revenue was $4.25 billion, representing a 46% increase year-over-year from $2.91 billion in the prior year. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of at least 40% year-over-year revenue expansion, surpassing our internal guidance midpoint and consensus estimates by about 4%. Our gross margin expanded 320 basis points to 22.4%, our highest ever, reflecting ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency through automation, supply chain resilience, and battery cost reductions. Operating expenses were controlled at $850 million, and net income came in at $420 million. We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet with $3.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents, plus a $1.5 billion undrawn revolver. Our guidance for Q4 is total revenue of $4.6 to $4.9 billion, implying 42-48% year-over-year growth, with full-year 2024 on track for $16.8 to $17.2 billion.

As we dive deeper into our top-line results, they underscore the resilience and momentum in our EV ecosystem amid a dynamic global market. Automotive revenue, our core segment, reached $3.72 billion, up 52% year-over-year, propelled by record vehicle deliveries of 185,000 units globally, a 28% increase and beating guidance by 5,000 units. This was driven by a 15% sequential ramp in our core SUV lineup, with average selling price holding steady at $52,000 overall, supporting these strong gross margins ahead of consensus, thanks to regulatory credit sales exceeding $185 million. Energy generation and storage revenue hit $320 million, surging 112% year-over-year from 2.8 GWh of Megapack-scale battery systems shipped, including a major 500 MWh project for a California utility. Services and other revenue was $210 million, up 31%, fueled by our Supercharger network now at 18,000 stalls with 25% utilization and OTA software upgrades like our Autonomy Suite v3.2 at 65% adoption.

Regionally, North America accounted for 68% of revenue at $2.91 billion, up 55% year-over-year, with U.S. deliveries at 92,000 units boosted by IRA tax credit eligibility up to $7,500 per vehicle. Europe contributed 22% at $935 million, up 38%, with strong traction in the UK and Norway despite subsidy phase-outs. Asia-Pacific was 10% or $425 million, up 22%, with our Shanghai JV delivering 15,000 units amid pricing pressures.

On average selling price trends by model and region, our global blended ASP was $52,400 for the quarter, down 8% year-over-year and 3% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting deliberate pricing to drive fleet wins and retail adoption, offset by mix shifts toward premium configurations. Excluding FX headwinds from a stronger USD, the underlying decline was about 6% year-over-year. This is disciplined compared to peers like Tesla's steeper drops or BYD's aggressive China pricing.

By model: NovaSUV, our flagship mid-size crossover at 60% mix, had ASP at $48,200, down 12% year-over-year due to a $3,500 cut on base RWD to counter competitors and capture IRA fleet share, but uplifted by 42% take rates on Enhanced Autopilot and optional 100 kWh packs adding $4,200 in options revenue. NovaSedan, 20% mix, held at $78,500 ASP, flat year-over-year with new Ultra trim at $85k featuring tri-motor power and 800V architecture. NovaOne entry-level hatchback, 10% mix, at $32,800 ASP, down 5%, priced aggressively at $29,990 base with LFP cells against BYD and VW. NovaTitan pickup, 10% mix, at $72,300 ASP, down 10% from a new RWD trim, bolstered by high-margin accessories.

Regionally: North America ASP $56,800, down 7%, shielded by IRA credits with 52% leasing mix; Europe $49,200, down 11% from tariffs and subsidy cliffs; China/APAC $38,500, down 15% versus local competition; rest of world stable at $51k. Mix shifts to 32% premium added $1,200 to blended ASP, with incentives at $2.8k per unit. We're guiding Q4 blended ASP to $51k-$53k, prioritizing margin-accretive growth via LFP shifts and ADAS subscriptions.

Before we move on, I'd like to provide a detailed update on delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 and into 2025. In Q3, we delivered 185,000 vehicles, up 28% year-over-year despite lithium price volatility. For Q4, we expect 210,000 to 220,000 units, 15-20% sequential growth and 35-40% year-over-year, implying full-year 2024 of 780,000 to 790,000, a 45% increase. By model: NovaSUV 130,000-135,000, up 18% sequentially with robust NA demand from NV-Pilot updates; NovaSedan 40,000-42,000 with structural packs reversing softness; NovaOne 22,000-24,000 post-launch; NovaTitan 18,000-19,000 ramping at Texas Gigafactory. Regionally: NA 65% (137k-143k), Europe 20%, China/APAC 15%. For full-year 2025, 1.1-1.2 million deliveries, 40-50% ramp, with SUV/pickup mix to 65%.

Shifting to battery costs per kWh and trends, a critical lever where packs are 30-40% of BOM. Our average pack cost was $78 per kWh in Q3, down 8% quarter-over-quarter and 22% year-over-year from $100+, ahead of GM/Ford at $110-120 per BloombergNEF. Trends: 2021 at $145/kWh, 2022 $118, 2023 $105, now $78 via Nevada ramp to 80 GWh at 96.5% yields. Drivers: scale with CATL/LGES contracts at $75-85 for 45% LFP mix; tech like silicon anodes, dry coating slashing 25% solvents, QuantumScape solid-state pilots targeting $60 by 2026, Redwood recycling at $40 equivalent; regional IRA credits netting $50-60/kWh in US. This dropped battery % of revenue to 18%, adding 320 bps to 22.4% margins. Guide $80/kWh FY2024, sub-$70 by 2026.

These efficiencies tie into our aggressive factory expansions and operational improvements, key growth drivers supercharging margins. We've committed $4.2 billion CapEx this year, 60% or $2.5 billion to expansions ramping capacity from 450,000 to 1.2 million by 2026, a 167% increase against 25% EV CAGR. North America: Nevada Gigafactory Phase 2 at 65% complete, adding 40 GWh LFP/NMC to 80 GWh by Q4 2025, IRA-compliant for NovaSUV/Sedan, targeting 40% $50k-$70k SUV share. Europe: $1.1 billion Hungary plant next month for 250,000 EuroDrive units, leveraging EU funds, near CATL. Asia: $900 million Shanghai bolt-on for 150,000 CityEV. Networked via EVOS digital twin, cutting commissioning 25%.

Efficiency gains: 1,200 ABB robots boosted throughput 38% to 6,200 welds/hour, labor to 12 hours/vehicle, OEE to 92%. Battery yields 96.5%, $12/kWh shaved via dry coating, cell-to-pack cut weight 8%/$450. Supply chain: 70% SiC vertical, 85% NA content, turns 8.2x freeing $450 million. Energy: 450 MW solar/Megapacks drop costs 28% to $0.042/kWh, emissions down 22% to 4.2 tons CO2e/vehicle. Q4 CapEx $1.2 billion, FCF positive $250 million. These build our moat in $1T EV TAM.

I'll now turn the call over to David Lee to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

David Lee:
Thank you, Sarah. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of NovaSUV and our full lineup. Building on the expansions Sarah outlined, we're implementing several initiatives to further improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce costs, including full rollout of AI predictive maintenance via Siemens MindSphere, which has slashed downtime 40%, and modular prefab for faster builds. Our OEE at 92% and vertical integration keep us on track to meet production targets for the year and hit 1.2 million capacity by 2026. We're executing at Tesla-levels while qualifying for all IRA benefits.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, on the factory expansions, can you elaborate on risks around Hungary timelines and how the EU Battery Regulation impacts your cell sourcing there?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, John. Great question. The Hungary site is on track for groundbreaking next month, fully leveraging the €3.4 billion Just Transition Fund for compliance. Proximity to CATL's Debrecen fab ensures localized prismatic cells, hitting 75% EU content from day one for Net-Zero Industry Act alignment. Risks like labor or permitting are minimal—costs 30% below Germany—and our EVOS platform simulates full lines virtually. No major delays expected, positioning us for 20% EBITDA margins against VW price wars.

Operator:
Next question from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 2:
Hi team, strong deliveries. Mike or Sarah, on Q4 volume guidance by model, how sensitive is NovaOne to Tesla's rumored $25k model, and what's the 2025 upside from robotaxi?

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, Lisa. NovaOne at $32,500 base is IRA-compliant and ZEV-optimized for California, with 70% US focus—early wins already. Tesla's Model 2 won't hit until later, but our LFP packs and Shanghai ramp give us cost edge at 85% utilization. Robotaxi unveil at CES 2025 could unlock $5 billion recurring via fleets, adding 10% to 2025 volumes alongside FSD licensing. Guidance assumes 10% market growth per BloombergNEF, but that's conservative.

Operator:
Our next question is from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
David, on operational efficiencies, how sustainable is the 92% OEE, and details on SiC vertical integration derisking chips?

David Lee:
Raj, thanks. 92% OEE is sustainable via Siemens MindSphere AI on 4680 winders—downtime down 40%, yields rivaling Panasonic. Arizona fab with Wolfspeed covers 70% SiC modules, insulating from TSMC issues post-2022 shortages. 85% NA content boosts IRA $45/kWh credits, with inventory turns at 8.2x. We'll hold mid-90s OEE scaling to 1.2 million units.

Operator:
Next from Emily Wong with Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Sarah, battery costs at $78/kWh is impressive—walk us through LFP mix evolution and solid-state timeline versus lithium volatility?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, spot on. LFP now 45% mix from 15% last year via CATL deals at sub-$70/kWh, blended for entry models like NovaOne. Lithium up 10% QoQ to $12k/ton hedged with sulfate processes and Lynas offtakes. Dry coating at 80% lines cuts 25%, recycling 5% packs at $40 equivalent. QuantumScape Phase 2 targets $60/kWh prototypes 2026—energy density +15%, no major volatility impact expected.

Operator:
Our final question from Tom Harris with RBC Capital.

Analyst 5:
Team, ASP down to $52.4k—how do you protect margins in China price wars, and Q4 regional mix details?

Sarah Chen:
Tom, good one. China ASP $38.5k reflects BYD/Nio pressure, but Shanghai JV 40% cost savings and NV-Pilot premium keep 15% uplift. Two RMB 15k cuts countered Xiaomi/Zeekr, but ASEAN like Thailand adds $42k on AeroMax. Q4 mix: NA 65%, Europe 20% tempered by tariffs offset by Berlin 20 GWh, APAC 15% premium exports. Premium mix to 32% and $2.8k credits preserve 25%+ margins long-term.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more, but that concludes our Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy—from capacity ramps and cost efficiencies to strong delivery growth and margin expansion—delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
